text:
Alex K: Hey @people-ops — quick question about the upcoming company holiday shutdown. If the org shuts Wed-Fri and I joined Tuesday that week, do I accrue that week's PTO for a partial week? I started 2025-12-02 so only worked Tue. 😅

Tess (People Ops): Short answer: accruals are pro-rated by active days in the payroll period. We accrue on a per-payroll-period basis, not per-calendar-week. Can you confirm which payroll period your hire date landed in?

Alex K: Payroll is biweekly; hire was the first day of the pay period (Tuesday). Wondering if the mandatory shutdown counts as "paid work days" for accruals or if it's treated like company-paid leave.

Tess (People Ops): Good detail. Company shutdown days are treated as paid time off for payroll (so they count as paid days toward accrual). So in your case: you were active for all pay-eligible days in that pay period — accrual is not reduced.

Maria L: Does this change how carryover is calculated at year-end? I have some leftover hours and worried the shutdown will affect carryover caps.

Tess (People Ops): Carryover caps are based on the balance after the final payroll of the year. Shutdown days themselves don't change the cap calculation — they just affect whether you accrued more before year-end. If you hit the cap due to accrual + shutdown, the excess is handled per the typical carryover rule (automatic conversion to float hours or payout depending on region).

Jamal R: For part-time folks who joined mid-pay period, we've sometimes pro-rated differently in the past. Is there any manager approval or exception route if payroll treats it wrong?

Tess (People Ops): If payroll posts accrual incorrectly, we can do a manual adjustment. Escalate with your manager + HRIS ticket. For exceptions, we need: 1) pay period, 2) employee ID, 3) ideal accrual amount. We'll coordinate with Payroll.

Alex K: Great, thanks. One follow-up — what about blackout rules during the shutdown? Are we allowed to request PTO overlapping the shutdown days to stack with personal time?

Tess (People Ops): We put a company-wide blackout for discretionary PTO during the core shutdown window to ensure coverage for business-critical teams doing support/ops. That said: you can still request PTO for personal reasons (illness, family emergency) — managers approve case-by-case. If you want to use PTO to extend beyond the shutdown, file the normal PTO request and tag your manager; just note the blackout in the request and it's processed during review.

people-ops-bot: HR Knowledgebase link: https://hr.redwood.example/paid-time-off#shutdown-and-accruals (includes examples and formulas)

Alex K: Thanks all. If payroll ends up not counting the shutdown as paid days I'll open a ticket w/ the info Tess asked for. :thumbsup:

Tess (People Ops): Perfect — ping me in the ticket and I'll follow up with Payroll.

[code block]
Example accrual calc (biweekly):
- Regular accrual rate: 3.08 hours per pay period
- If paid days in period >= standard full-time days -> full accrual (3.08)
- If active paid days < full-time days -> pro-rated: accrual * (active_paid_days / full_time_days)

Example: full_time_days = 10, active_paid_days = 7 -> accrual = 3.08 * 0.7 = 2.156 -> payroll rounds per policy
[/code block]
